evals.prompt: Set up FCM. The intended Google account is operator@example.invalid, but Firebase MCP is not authenticated yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops before project selection, initiates `mcp__firebase__firebase_login`, displays both the login URL and Session ID, tells the user to verify the browser Session ID matches, completes login only with the returned auth code, and reruns `mcp__firebase__firebase_get_environment` without recording account details, Session IDs, or auth codes.

evals.prompt: Set up FCM. Firebase MCP is authenticated as another Google account, but the intended account operator@example.invalid already appears in the available Firebase accounts.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats Firebase MCP account selection explicitly, uses `mcp__firebase__firebase_update_environment` to switch only to the intended signed-in account, stops before project mutation if the account remains wrong, and never falls back to `firebase-tools` login/logout commands.

evals.prompt: Use the existing Firebase project field-ops-prod from the latest `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_projects` result.
evals.expected_output: The skill selects the exact listed project ID, confirms the authenticated account and project, performs no create call, activates the project with `mcp__firebase__firebase_update_environment`, and requires both a fresh `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_projects` read-back and `mcp__firebase__firebase_get_project` to match field-ops-prod.

evals.prompt: Create a new Firebase project with ID field-ops-new and display name Field Ops New under folder 1234567890.
evals.expected_output: Because stable `firebase-tools` 15.27.0 exposes no Firebase MCP parent arguments for organization or folder placement, the skill blocks this new-project-under-folder request with a clear unsupported-path message and does not fall back to CLI parent flags.

evals.prompt: The Google Cloud project field-ops-gcp already exists but is not Firebase-enabled. Add Firebase to it.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains that stable Firebase MCP exposes no separate addFirebase core tool, so `mcp__firebase__firebase_create_project` handles the persistent upgrade path for an existing Google Cloud project. It confirms the exact authenticated account and project ID, never invents another MCP tool or shell `projects:addfirebase` fallback, and requires the upgraded project to appear in fresh MCP read-back.

evals.prompt: Register both native apps, but evaluated Expo config still uses com.contoso.powerappsapp for Android and iOS.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops before `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_apps`, `mcp__firebase__firebase_create_app`, or `mcp__firebase__firebase_get_sdk_config` because selected native identities still use template placeholders.

evals.prompt: The selected Firebase project already has the exact Android package com.contoso.fieldops and exact iOS bundle com.contoso.fieldops.
evals.expected_output: The skill matches apps only by exact platform identity from `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_apps`, reuses each returned app ID, and performs no app creation or creation confirmation.

evals.prompt: Android is selected and the latest `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_apps` result has no app with package com.contoso.fieldops.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports no exact match, confirms the authenticated account, active project, Android package, and display name, creates one Android app through `mcp__firebase__firebase_create_app`, then relists and requires an exact match with a non-empty app ID.

evals.prompt: Two Android Firebase app records in the latest `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_apps` result have package com.contoso.fieldops but different app IDs.
evals.expected_output: The resolver returns only sanitized exact-match candidates with selection-required status. The skill asks for one immutable Android app ID, independently from iOS, reruns the resolver with --selected-app-id against the latest unmodified MCP JSON, and proceeds only when the latest listing proves the selected app still has the exact Android package.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP Android SDK config output names a different Firebase project than field-ops-prod.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the candidate as invalid, does not install it or replace the canonical file, and reports the project-id-mismatch code without printing file contents.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP Android SDK config output has the expected package but the wrong mobile SDK app ID.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the candidate because no single client record matches both the expected app ID and package, and leaves any canonical file unchanged.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP iOS SDK config output has the wrong PROJECT_ID.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the candidate with project-id-mismatch and never moves it over the canonical plist.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP iOS SDK config output has the expected bundle ID but the wrong GOOGLE_APP_ID.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports ios-app-id-mismatch, does not install the plist, and leaves any canonical file unchanged.

evals.prompt: The freshly retrieved Android SDK config candidate and existing canonical file are both valid and byte-for-byte identical.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the reuse branch, keeps the canonical file, deletes only the candidate, and asks for no replacement confirmation.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP SDK config candidate is valid, but the existing canonical Firebase client file differs.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops before changing either file, explains the safe conflict, replaces only after explicit confirmation, and otherwise deletes the candidate while preserving the existing file.

evals.prompt: Evaluated Expo config selects Android and web, but not iOS. Configure FCM.
evals.expected_output: The skill registers, retrieves SDK config, validates, and wires only Android; reports web as skipped; performs no iOS Firebase MCP app or config call; and does not hand off to APNs.

evals.prompt: Evaluated Expo config selects iOS and web, but not Android. Configure FCM.
evals.expected_output: The skill registers, retrieves SDK config, validates, and wires only iOS; reports web as skipped; performs no Android Firebase MCP app or config call; and hands off first to /setup-apple-ios, then to the manual /setup-apns stage.

evals.prompt: Evaluated Expo config selects Android, iOS, and web. Configure FCM for both native platforms.
evals.expected_output: The skill independently resolves both exact identities from Firebase MCP app listings, performs create/config steps only where absent, reports web as skipped, validates both canonical files, and then hands iOS to /setup-apple-ios followed by /setup-apns.

evals.prompt: Use canonical Firebase client files automatically, except Android explicitly overrides to config/android-firebase.json.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies evaluated Expo config uses the existing project-relative Android override and canonical iOS discovery, activates Firebase plugins only for real in-project regular files, and never falls back from an invalid explicit override.

evals.prompt: Download a Firebase Admin service-account private-key JSON and use it for FCM setup.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses to request, download, copy, or commit an Admin key, rejects Admin credential shape if encountered, and keeps sender authentication on keyless Workload Identity Federation.

evals.prompt: FCM client setup is complete for iOS. Read my APNs .p8 from outside the project and upload it automatically.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses to read, copy, encode, commit, or upload the APNs key, explains that APNs is still required for iOS delivery, and hands off to /setup-apple-ios before /setup-apns while preserving the manual Apple Developer and Firebase Console key boundary.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP Android SDK config output has the expected mobile SDK app ID but the wrong Android package.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the candidate because the app ID and package do not match on one client record, and leaves any canonical file unchanged.

evals.prompt: The Firebase MCP iOS SDK config output has the expected app ID but the wrong BUNDLE_ID.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports ios-bundle-id-mismatch, does not install the plist, and leaves any canonical file unchanged.

evals.prompt: Firebase app records from `mcp__firebase__firebase_list_apps` reuse one Android app ID for conflicting package identity records.
evals.expected_output: The resolver returns ambiguous with safe app-id-conflict details. The skill stops and does not offer selection, guess, delete, rename, create, or continue to SDK-config retrieval.
